verses.zh: （一篇诗歌，交与伶长。）全地都当向　神欢呼！
verses.en: For the music director, a song, a psalm.Shout out praise to God, all the earth!

verses.zh: 歌颂他名的荣耀！用赞美的言语将他的荣耀发明！
verses.en: Sing praises about the majesty of his reputation.[NOTE:1] Give him the honor he deserves![NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 66. The psalmist praises God because he has delivered his people from a crisis.
Heb “his name,” which here stands metonymically for God’s reputation.

verses.zh: 当对　神说：你的作为何等可畏！因你的大能，仇敌要投降你。
verses.en: Say to God:“How awesome are your deeds!Because of your great power your enemies cower in fear[NOTE:1] before you.
notes: Heb “make honorable his praise.”

verses.zh: 全地要敬拜你，歌颂你，要歌颂你的名。（细拉）
verses.en: All the earth worships[NOTE:1] youand sings praises to you.They sing praises to your name.” (Selah)
notes: See Deut 33:29; Ps 81:15 for other uses of the verb כָּחַשׁ (kakhash) in the sense “cower in fear.” In Ps 18:44 the verb seems to carry the nuance “be weak, powerless” (see also Ps 109:24).

verses.zh: 你们来看　神所行的，他向世人所做之事是可畏的。
verses.en: Come and witness[NOTE:1] God’s exploits![NOTE:2] His acts on behalf of people are awesome.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “bows down to.” The prefixed verbal forms in v. 4 are taken (1) as imperfects expressing what is typical. Another option (2) is to interpret them as anticipatory (“all the earth will worship you”) or (3) take them as jussives, expressing a prayer or wish (“may all the earth worship you”).
Or “see.”
Or “acts” (see Ps 46:8).

verses.zh: 他将海变成干地，众民步行过河；我们在那里因他欢喜。
verses.en: He turned the sea into dry land;[NOTE:1] they passed through the river on foot.[NOTE:2] Let us rejoice in him there.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “awesome [is] an act toward the sons of man.” It is unclear how the prepositional phrase relates to what precedes. If collocated with “act,” it may mean “on behalf of” or “toward.” If taken with “awesome” (see 1 Chr 16:25; Pss 89:7; 96:4; Zeph 2:11), one might translate “his awesome acts are beyond human comprehension” or “his awesome acts are superior to anything men can do.”
He turned the sea into dry land. The psalmist alludes to Israel’s crossing the Red Sea (Exod 14:21).

Because of the reference to “the river,” some understand this as an allusion to Israel’s crossing the Jordan River. However, the Hebrew term נָהָר (nahad) does not always refer to a “river” in the technical sense; it can be used of sea currents (see Jonah 2:4). So this line may also refer to the Red Sea crossing (cf. NEB).

verses.zh: 他用权能治理万民，直到永远。他的眼睛鉴察列邦；悖逆的人不可自高。（细拉）
verses.en: He rules[NOTE:1] by his power forever;he watches[NOTE:2] the nations.Stubborn rebels should not exalt[NOTE:3] themselves. (Selah)
notes: The adverb שָׁם (sham, “there”) is used here, as often in poetic texts, to point “to a spot in which a scene is localized vividly in the imagination” (BDB 1027 s.v.).
Heb “[the] one who rules.”
Heb “his eyes watch.” “Eyes” are an anthropomorphism, attributed to God here to emphasize his awareness of all that happens on earth.

verses.zh: 万民哪，你们当称颂我们的　神，使人得听赞美他的声音。
verses.en: Praise[NOTE:1] our God, you nations.Loudly proclaim his praise.[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb form is jussive (note the negative particle אַל, ʾal). The Kethib (consonantal text) has a Hiphil form of the verb, apparently to be understood in an exhibitive sense (“demonstrate stubborn rebellion”; see BDB 927 s.v. רוּם Hiph), while the Qere (marginal reading) has a Qal form, to be understood in an intransitive sense. The preposition ל (lamed) with pronominal suffix should be understood in a reflexive sense (“for themselves”) and indicates that the action is performed with the interest of the subject in mind.
Heb “bless,” in the sense of declaring “God to be the source of…special power” (see HALOT 160 s.v. II ברך pi).

verses.zh: 他使我们的性命存活，也不叫我们的脚摇动。
verses.en: He preserves our lives[NOTE:1] and does not allow our feet to slip.
notes: Heb “cause the voice of his praise to be heard.”

verses.zh: 神啊，你曾试验我们，熬炼我们，如熬炼银子一样。
verses.en: For[NOTE:1] you, O God, tested us;you purified us like refined silver.
notes: Heb “the one who places our soul in life.”

verses.zh: 你使我们进入网罗，把重担放在我们的身上。
verses.en: You led us into a trap;[NOTE:1] you caused us to suffer.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “indeed.”
Heb “you brought us into a net.” This rare word for “net” also occurs in Ezek 12:13; 13:21; 17:20.

verses.zh: 你使人坐车轧我们的头；我们经过水火，你却使我们到丰富之地。
verses.en: You allowed men to ride over our heads;we passed through fire and water,but you brought us out into a wide open place.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you placed suffering on our hips.” The noun מוּעָקָה (muʿaqah, “suffering”) occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 我要用燔祭进你的殿，向你还我的愿，
verses.en: I will enter[NOTE:1] your temple with burnt sacrifices;I will fulfill the vows I made to you,
notes: The MT reads רְוָיָה (revayah, “saturation”) but this should be emended to רְוָחָה (revakhah, “wide open place”; i.e., “relief”), a reading supported by several ancient versions (LXX, Syriac, Jerome, Targum).

verses.zh: 就是在急难时我嘴唇所发的、口中所许的。
verses.en: which my lips utteredand my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.

verses.zh: 我要把肥牛作燔祭，将公羊的香祭献给你，又把公牛和山羊献上。（细拉）
verses.en: I will offer up to you fattened animals as burnt sacrifices,along with the smell of sacrificial rams.I will offer cattle and goats. (Selah)

verses.zh: 凡敬畏　神的人，你们都来听！我要述说他为我所行的事。
verses.en: Come! Listen, all you who are loyal to God.[NOTE:1] I will declare what he has done for me.
notes: Here the psalmist switches to the singular; he speaks as the representative of the nation.

verses.zh: 我曾用口求告他；我的舌头也称他为高。
verses.en: I cried out to him for help[NOTE:1] and praised him with my tongue.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “all of the fearers of God.”
Heb “to him [with] my mouth I called.”

verses.zh: 我若心里注重罪孽，主必不听。
verses.en: If I had harbored sin in my heart,[NOTE:1] the Lord would not have listened.
notes: Heb “and he was extolled under my tongue.” The form רוֹמַם (romam) appears to be a Polal (passive) participle from רוּם (rum, “be exalted”), but many prefer to read רוֹמָם, “high praise [was under my tongue]” (cf. NEB). See BDB 928 s.v. רוֹמָם.

verses.zh: 但　神实在听见了；他侧耳听了我祷告的声音。
verses.en: However, God heard;he listened to my prayer.

verses.zh: 神是应当称颂的！他并没有推却我的祷告，也没有叫他的慈爱离开我。
verses.en: God deserves praise,[NOTE:1] for[NOTE:2] he did not reject my prayeror abandon his love for me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “sin if I had seen in my heart.”
Heb “blessed [be] God.”
Or “who.” In a blessing formula after בָּרוּךְ (barukh, “blessed be”) the form אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher), whether taken as a relative pronoun or causal particle, introduces the basis for the blessing/praise.
